name: theme
title: Interlace Theme
description: @interlace/ui — full DS CSS baseline: tokens, foundation (type/spacing/radius), preflight (focus ring + min-viewport contract), shadcn↔fumadocs bridge, and brand palette.
author: ofri-peretz <https://github.com/ofri-peretz>

files.content:
/*
 * @interlace/ui — canonical Interlace brand theme (light + dark).
 *
 * Imported by `index.css` (the canonical barrel). Direct consumer import is
 * still supported for backward-compat, but new consumers should prefer:
 *
 *   @import "@interlace/ui/styles/index.css";   // ← one line, full contract
 *
 * Why this file exists separately from theme.css:
 *
 *   - `theme.css` is the **bridge** layer — maps shadcn-bare tokens (`--card`,
 *     `--popover`) to whatever the surrounding framework exposes
 *     (`--color-fd-*` from fumadocs, in this project).
 *   - `interlace-theme.css` is the **brand** layer — concrete hex values that
 *     identify this product. App consumers who fork the brand override the
 *     `@layer interlace.brand` block (see `THEME_AUTHORING.md` once it lands);
 *     the bridge layer (`theme.css`) stays.
 *
 * ─── Two orthogonal axes: scheme × theme ──────────────────────────
 *
 * A colour SCHEME and a THEME are different questions and must not share a
 * selector. Until Phase 8 they did: the dark block was keyed on
 * `.dark, [data-theme='dark']`, which spends the `data-theme` attribute —
 * the only obvious place to put "which brand" — on "which scheme".
 *
 *   scheme  →  light | dark              (`.dark` / `[data-scheme='dark']`)
 *   theme   →  interlace | harbor | …    (`[data-theme='<name>']`)
 *
 * | Selector                        | Means                                |
 * |---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
 * | `:root`                         | interlace · light  (the default)     |
 * | `.dark`, `[data-scheme='dark']` | interlace · dark                     |
 * | `[data-theme='X']`              | theme X · light   (themes/X.css)     |
 * | `[data-theme='X'].dark`         | theme X · dark    (themes/X.css)     |
 *
 * `.dark` stays load-bearing on purpose: it is the shadcn / next-themes
 * convention, every consumer and the Storybook `withThemeByClassName`
 * decorator write it, and breaking it to gain a cleaner name would be
 * vanity. The new axis is purely ADDITIVE — nothing that worked before
 * stopped working, with one deliberate exception: `[data-theme='dark']` no
 * longer means "dark scheme". It now reads as "the theme named dark", which
 * is not a registered theme, so it resolves to interlace · light. Consumers
 * on that spelling move to `[data-scheme='dark']` (or `.dark`).
 *
 * Every theme file declares into `@layer interlace.brand` and overrides ONLY
 * `--interlace-*` hex values. The semantics layer below and the
 * `@theme inline` block never change — that is the whole point of the
 * cascade, and it is why a theme is a data file rather than a pile of CSS.
 * `THEME_TOKENS` (src/lib/theme-tokens.ts) enumerates every token a theme
 * must define, and `__tests__/theme-contract-lock.test.ts` fails on a theme
 * that omits one — because a missing token does not throw, it silently
 * inherits the PREVIOUS theme's value and ships a two-brand page nobody
 * notices.
 *
 * ─── Layer model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 *
 * This file declares content into TWO cascade layers:
 *
 *   @layer interlace.brand     — concrete hex values (--interlace-* literals).
 *                                Light + dark mode color palettes. THE
 *                                supported consumer override surface.
 *
 *   @layer interlace.semantics — semantic alias bindings (--background,
 *                                --foreground, --muted-foreground, ...) that
 *                                resolve to the brand layer's --interlace-*
 *                                via `var()`. Tailwind v4 `@theme inline`
 *                                stays at the top level (NOT wrapped in a
 *                                custom layer) because Tailwind processes
 *                                that directive globally to emit utilities.
 *
 * Contrast contract (WCAG 2.2 AA):
 *   - Body text on background: ≥ 4.5:1 (target: 7:1 AAA where possible)
 *   - Large text + UI controls on adjacent surface: ≥ 3:1
 *   - Focus ring on adjacent colors: ≥ 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13)
 *   - Verified at https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/ — every
 *     primary/foreground pair below clears the floor for its mode.
 *
 * Source palette: the Interlace mark — burnt orange (see render-cover.sh).
 *   Light primary: #7d350c → 8.80:1 on white (AAA)
 *   Dark primary:  #fbb99a → 11.79:1 on near-black (AAA)
 *
 * Replaced the Tailwind-violet palette this system shipped with. Every pair
 * below was re-measured after the swap; none regressed.
 */

@layer interlace.brand {
  /* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *  LIGHT — default
   * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  :root {
    /* Brand
     *
     * Burnt orange, from the mark. #7d350c measures 8.80:1 on white, 8.12:1
     * on `--accent` (#fef4ed), and 7.46:1 on its OWN 10% tint — that last one
     * is the binding constraint. `bg-primary/10` + `text-primary` is a stock
     * shadcn badge pattern, and it composites to #f3ebe7 on white; a lighter
     * orange (#8a3a10) landed at 6.63:1 there and axe failed the enhanced
     * check. This value tracks violet-800's old profile (8.98 / 7.56) so the
     * AAA floor holds on every catalogue surface AND on brand-tinted ones. */
    --interlace-primary: #7d350c;            /* 8.80:1 on white (AAA) */
    --interlace-primary-hover: #6b2b09;      /* 10.63:1 on white */
    --interlace-primary-active: #4d2009;     /* 13.76:1 on white */
    --interlace-primary-foreground: #ffffff;
    --interlace-primary-subtle: #fef4ed;     /* warm tint for backgrounds */
    --interlace-primary-subtle-foreground: #4d2009;  /* 12.70:1 on subtle (AAA) */

    /* Surface */
    --interlace-background: #ffffff;
    --interlace-foreground: #0d0b09;         /* near-black, slight warm tint */
    --interlace-card: #ffffff;
    --interlace-card-foreground: #0d0b09;
    --interlace-popover: #ffffff;
    --interlace-popover-foreground: #0d0b09;
    --interlace-muted: #faf7f4;              /* warm-tinted neutral */
    --interlace-muted-foreground: #4d453c;   /* 8.06:1 on white (AAA body); darkened from #6b6580 to clear AA even under axe sub-pixel rounding on hairline text */
    --interlace-border: #eae7e2;    /* 1.23:1 on white — decorative separators only, exempt from 1.4.11 */
    /* `--input` is the BOUNDARY of a form control (input / textarea / select
     * trigger / checkbox / radio / switch track), so WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11
     * (Non-text Contrast, AA) demands ≥3:1 against the adjacent surface —
     * the border is the only thing identifying the control.
     *
     * It used to alias `--border` (#eae7e2 → 1.23:1 on white): every
     * unfocused field in the DS was effectively invisible to a low-vision
     * user. Forked to a warm mid-grey that clears the floor while keeping
     * the brand's warm cast. Decorative `--border` deliberately stays soft. */
    --interlace-input: #8f857a;              /* 3.62:1 on white (SC 1.4.11 AA) */
    --interlace-ring: var(--interlace-primary);

    /* Accent */
    --interlace-accent: #fef4ed;             /* warm tint */
    --interlace-accent-foreground: #73300d;  /* 8.98:1 on accent (AAA) */

    /* Secondary */
    --interlace-secondary: #f5f3f0;
    --interlace-secondary-foreground: #1f1a15;

    /* Destructive (Tailwind red-800 — bumped from red-700 #b91c1c (6.4:1) so
     * text-destructive on white clears WCAG 2.2 AAA (≥7:1) for normal body
     * text. red-800 #991b1b ≈ 8.0:1. */
    --interlace-destructive: #991b1b;
    --interlace-destructive-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Success (Tailwind emerald-800 — bumped from emerald-600 #059669 (3.7:1).
     * text-success on white now ≈ 7.3:1, clearing AAA. The original brand
     * green stays available for bg-success surfaces (paired with white
     * foreground) where the contrast is between surface and foreground, not
     * surface and parent. */
    --interlace-success: #065f46;
    --interlace-success-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Warning (Tailwind amber-900 — bumped from amber-600 #d97706 (3.5:1).
     * Yellow on white can't physically clear 7:1 at its brand-bright value,
     * so the text token drops to amber-900 #78350f ≈ 8.5:1. For "yellow
     * background" treatments, pair `bg-amber-500` (decorative bg) with
     * `text-warning` (this token) — contrast is then warning on amber, not
     * warning on white. */
    --interlace-warning: #78350f;
    --interlace-warning-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Info (Tailwind blue-800 — new semantic token. text-info on white ≈
     * 8.5:1, AAA. Pair with bg-info-foreground for filled surfaces. */
    --interlace-info: #1e40af;
    --interlace-info-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Caution — the rung BETWEEN warning and destructive. Scorecard ladders
     * need five distinguishable tones (excellent / good / fair / poor /
     * fail); without this token `poor` had no home and GradeBadge reached
     * outside the palette for a raw `bg-orange-900`. Tailwind orange-900
     * #7c2d12 ≈ 9.0:1 on white and stays hue-distinct from `--warning`
     * (amber-900 #78350f) at a glance while sharing the warm family. */
    --interlace-caution: #7c2d12;
    --interlace-caution-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Scrim — the dark wash laid over an arbitrary image so text on top
     * stays legible (featured article covers, media overlays). Like the
     * hero surface these do NOT invert: the scrim's whole job is to be
     * darker than whatever photo sits under it, in either colour scheme.
     * Always used with a Tailwind alpha modifier (`bg-scrim/70`) — the
     * solid values are the ramp's endpoints, not what ships on screen.
     * #ffffff on #000000/70 over a mid-tone cover measures ≥ 7:1. */
    --interlace-scrim: #000000;
    --interlace-scrim-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Cosmic hero effects — the three colours the starfield preset paints
     * onto <canvas> / SVG gradients (shooting-star head, its trail, meteor
     * streak). They live in the brand layer because the hero is the most
     * brand-visible surface we ship, and because canvas ignores the
     * cascade: HeroCosmic resolves these at runtime rather than letting a
     * vendored default paint the pre-brand violet palette (R19).
     *
     * The hero always renders on a deep near-black gradient in BOTH modes
     * (it is its own surface, not a themed one), so these do not invert. */
    --interlace-hero-star: #fbb99a;   /* brand orange tint — star head */
    --interlace-hero-trail: #0d9460;  /* brand green — trail gradient */
    --interlace-hero-meteor: #fdd6c2; /* palest orange — meteor streak */

    /* Cosmic hero surface. The hero is its OWN surface, not a themed one:
     * a starfield only reads as a starfield on near-black, so these do not
     * invert with the colour scheme. That is exactly why they need their
     * own tokens — reaching for `--background` / `--foreground` here would
     * paint black text on a black hero in light mode (the bug this pair
     * replaces). #f0ede9 on #0d0b09 measures 16.4:1 (AAA). */
    --interlace-hero-surface: #0d0b09;      /* gradient midpoint */
    --interlace-hero-surface-deep: #000000; /* gradient floor */
    --interlace-hero-foreground: #f0ede9;   /* 16.4:1 on the surface (AAA) */

    /* Window controls — the three macOS traffic-light dots used by the
     * CodeWindow chrome. Purely decorative (the dot row is `aria-hidden`),
     * but they live here so a consumer forking the brand can restyle the
     * chrome without patching component source. Values are the macOS
     * system colours the affordance is quoting. */
    --interlace-window-control-close: #ff5f57;
    --interlace-window-control-minimize: #febc2e;
    --interlace-window-control-zoom: #28c840;

    /* Chart palette — five distinct hues for series colors, brand-owned
     * so consumers can fork via `@layer interlace.brand`. Values match the
     * existing oklch ladder in theme.css (≥4.5:1 on bg-card light); the
     * promotion here makes the chart series an explicit brand surface
     * with `@layer interlace.brand` override semantics like every other
     * brand-coupled token. */
    --interlace-chart-1: oklch(0.55 0.16 41);   /* brand orange */
    --interlace-chart-2: oklch(0.55 0.14 162);  /* brand green */
    --interlace-chart-3: oklch(0.55 0.18 264);  /* blue */
    --interlace-chart-4: oklch(0.55 0.14 90);   /* olive */
    --interlace-chart-5: oklch(0.55 0.13 200);  /* cyan */

    /* Visualisation chrome — the parts of a chart that are NOT the series.
     *
     * `--chart-N` answers "which line is which". These answer "what is the
     * line drawn on": gridlines, axis, graph edges. Three hex values; every
     * other `--viz-*` token in the semantics layer is a var() alias of an
     * already-AA-verified token, so a brand fork has three numbers to pick,
     * not fifteen. Warm-neutral to sit with the brand, not the cool greys.
     *
     * Contrast, measured against `--interlace-background` #ffffff (which is
     * also `--interlace-card` in light mode):
     *   grid  #e0dad2 → 1.39:1  DECORATIVE. Gridlines must never be the sole
     *                           carrier of a value — that is what the axis
     *                           labels and the sr-only table are for. Kept
     *                           deliberately below 3:1 so a dense grid does
     *                           not fight the series it exists to support.
     *   axis  #8d857a → 3.64:1  Clears WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 (3:1, non-text UI
     *                           boundary). The axis IS structural — it is what
     *                           tells you where zero is.
     *   edge  #e0dad2 → 1.39:1  Ambient graph texture, same weight as grid.
     *                           An edge that MEANS something (selected, on the
     *                           highlighted path) switches to `--viz-edge-active`
     *                           (= `--primary`). Same split as the slider rail
     *                           vs knob: the low-contrast element is
     *                           supplementary, the high-contrast one carries
     *                           the success criterion. */
    --interlace-viz-grid: #e0dad2;
    --interlace-viz-axis: #8d857a;
    --interlace-viz-edge: #e0dad2;

    /* Radii (8/12/16 — three-step scale) */
    --interlace-radius-sm: 0.5rem;   /*  8px */
    --interlace-radius-md: 0.75rem;  /* 12px */
    --interlace-radius-lg: 1rem;     /* 16px */

    /* Brand mark — bar fills for the two-bar Interlace mark (nav lockups;
     * see packages/ui/src/patterns/brand-logo.tsx). Decorative fills, not
     * text, so they track the favicon pair rather than the AAA text ramp.
     * Values match the eslint.interlace.tools nav mark. */
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-o: #a84c17;
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-g: #0a6b47;
  }

  /* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *  INTERLACE · DARK — the scheme axis.
   *
   *  `.dark` is the shadcn / next-themes class every consumer already
   *  writes; `[data-scheme='dark']` is the attribute spelling for hosts
   *  that would rather not touch className. They are the SAME axis, and
   *  neither of them says anything about which brand is active — that is
   *  `[data-theme]`, handled in styles/themes/*.css.
   * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .dark,
  [data-scheme='dark'] {
    /* Brand — inverted weight: a light tint of the same burnt orange, so
     * both directions clear AAA. text-primary on near-black is 11.79:1, and
     * bg-primary with text-primary-foreground (#0a0a0a) is the same 11.79:1.
     * The cover orange #f4794a is only 7.24:1 here, too dark to carry the
     * bidirectional pair, hence the lighter tint. */
    --interlace-primary: #fbb99a;            /* 11.79:1 on dark bg (AAA) */
    --interlace-primary-hover: #fcc9b0;      /* 13.31:1 */
    --interlace-primary-active: #fdd6c2;     /* 14.68:1 */
    --interlace-primary-foreground: #0a0a0a; /* near-black — 11.79:1 on primary */
    --interlace-primary-subtle: #3d1a08;     /* tinted background */
    --interlace-primary-subtle-foreground: #fdd6c2;  /* 11.54:1 on subtle (AAA) */

    /* Surface */
    --interlace-background: #0a0a0a;
    --interlace-foreground: #f0ede9;
    --interlace-card: #171412;
    --interlace-card-foreground: #f0ede9;
    --interlace-popover: #171412;
    --interlace-popover-foreground: #f0ede9;
    --interlace-muted: #171412;
    --interlace-muted-foreground: #c9c3bb;   /* 9.6:1 on #0a0a0a (AAA); brightened from #a09cb3 (4.94:1) to clear AA even when stories render against `bg-fd-card/50` tinted surfaces */
    --interlace-border: #252019;    /* 1.22:1 on near-black — decorative separators only */
    /* Dark counterpart of the SC 1.4.11 fork above. #252019 measured
     * 1.22:1 on `--background` — same invisible-control failure as light. */
    --interlace-input: #6b635a;              /* 3.35:1 on #0a0a0a (SC 1.4.11 AA) */
    --interlace-ring: var(--interlace-primary);

    /* Accent */
    --interlace-accent: #3d1a08;             /* deep warm tint */
    --interlace-accent-foreground: #fcc9b0;  /* 10.46:1 on accent (AAA) */

    /* Secondary */
    --interlace-secondary: #201c17;
    --interlace-secondary-foreground: #f0ede9;

    /* Destructive (red-300 — bumped from red-500 #ef4444 (~5.2:1) so
     * text-destructive on near-black clears AAA. red-300 #fca5a5 ≈ 9:1. */
    --interlace-destructive: #fca5a5;
    --interlace-destructive-foreground: #0a0a0a;

    /* Success (emerald-400 — bumped from emerald-500 #10b981 (~6.3:1) for
     * AAA on dark. emerald-400 #34d399 ≈ 8.5:1. */
    --interlace-success: #34d399;
    --interlace-success-foreground: #052e16;

    /* Warning (amber-500 — already 7.7:1 on near-black, AAA. No bump needed
     * because yellows are physically easier on dark backgrounds than on light). */
    --interlace-warning: #f59e0b;
    --interlace-warning-foreground: #1e1b2e;

    /* Info (blue-300 — new semantic. text-info on near-black ≈ 8.7:1 (AAA). */
    --interlace-info: #93c5fd;
    --interlace-info-foreground: #0a0a0a;

    /* Caution (orange-300 — the dark-mode twin of the light orange-900 rung.
     * #fdba74 ≈ 10.9:1 on near-black; against its own `--caution-foreground`
     * (#0a0a0a) the filled chip reads the same 10.9:1, so the pair holds in
     * both directions like every other status token here. */
    --interlace-caution: #fdba74;
    --interlace-caution-foreground: #0a0a0a;

    /* ── Scheme-invariant tokens, restated ──────────────────────────
     * The nine tokens below plus the three radii hold the SAME value in
     * both schemes — a scrim is dark because it sits on a photo, and the
     * cosmic hero paints its own near-black surface in either scheme (see
     * the light block for the full reasoning on each).
     *
     * They are restated here anyway, following the precedent the window
     * controls set below: every theme × scheme block is a COMPLETE
     * override surface. That is what makes `THEME_TOKENS` checkable — a
     * per-scheme block that only carries the tokens which happen to
     * invert gives a forking consumer no way to tell "deliberately the
     * same" apart from "forgotten", and the lock no way to tell either. */
    --interlace-scrim: #000000;
    --interlace-scrim-foreground: #ffffff;

    --interlace-hero-star: #fbb99a;   /* brand orange tint — star head */
    --interlace-hero-trail: #0d9460;  /* brand green — trail gradient */
    --interlace-hero-meteor: #fdd6c2; /* palest orange — meteor streak */

    --interlace-hero-surface: #0d0b09;      /* gradient midpoint */
    --interlace-hero-surface-deep: #000000; /* gradient floor */
    --interlace-hero-foreground: #f0ede9;   /* 16.4:1 on the surface (AAA) */

    /* Radii (8/12/16 — three-step scale) */
    --interlace-radius-sm: 0.5rem;   /*  8px */
    --interlace-radius-md: 0.75rem;  /* 12px */
    --interlace-radius-lg: 1rem;     /* 16px */

    /* Window controls — macOS ships the same traffic-light hues in dark
     * mode, so these do not invert. Declared here anyway so the dark block
     * is a complete override surface for a forking consumer. */
    --interlace-window-control-close: #ff5f57;
    --interlace-window-control-minimize: #febc2e;
    --interlace-window-control-zoom: #28c840;

    /* Chart palette — lifted lightness so each series stays ≥4.5:1 on
     * `bg-card` (near-black). Same five hues as light, repositioned for
     * dark surfaces. */
    --interlace-chart-1: oklch(0.78 0.14 41);   /* brand orange */
    --interlace-chart-2: oklch(0.78 0.12 162);  /* brand green */
    --interlace-chart-3: oklch(0.78 0.16 264);  /* blue */
    --interlace-chart-4: oklch(0.78 0.12 90);   /* olive */
    --interlace-chart-5: oklch(0.78 0.11 200);  /* cyan */

    /* Visualisation chrome — dark. Measured against BOTH dark surfaces,
     * because a chart normally renders inside a Card, not on the page:
     *   grid  #2d2823 → 1.36:1 on bg / 1.26:1 on card   DECORATIVE
     *   axis  #746c60 → 3.82:1 on bg / 3.54:1 on card   clears SC 1.4.11 on both
     *   edge  #2d2823 → 1.36:1 on bg / 1.26:1 on card   ambient
     * Perceptual weight matched to light mode (1.39 / 3.64 / 1.39) so a grid
     * does not read as heavier in one theme than the other. */
    --interlace-viz-grid: #2d2823;
    --interlace-viz-axis: #746c60;
    --interlace-viz-edge: #2d2823;

    /* Brand mark — brighter pair for dark chrome (favicon dark variant). */
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-o: #f4794a;
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-g: #0d9460;
  }
}

@layer interlace.semantics {
  /* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *  Bind brand tokens to the shadcn-bare semantic names. Apps that want
   *  to override individual semantic values can re-declare them either
   *  here (`@layer interlace.semantics { :root { --background: ... } }`)
   *  AFTER importing this file, or they can fork the entire brand layer
   *  upstream (`@layer interlace.brand { ... }`) to swap the underlying
   *  hex values without touching the alias graph.
   *
   *  WHY FOUR SELECTORS AND NOT JUST `:root`. A custom property whose
   *  value is a `var()` is substituted at computed-value time on the
   *  element that DECLARES it, then inherited as a resolved value. So
   *  `:root { --primary: var(--interlace-primary) }` freezes whatever
   *  `--interlace-primary` is on the root. If a subtree re-brands itself
   *  (`<div class="dark">` — which is exactly what a Storybook decorator
   *  or a side-by-side theme preview does), the brand token changes on
   *  that div while `--primary` stays frozen at the root's value, and
   *  nothing repaints. Re-binding on every element that can carry a brand
   *  override is what makes subtree theming work.
   *
   *  `[data-theme]` is attribute-presence, not a value match: it covers
   *  every theme file that ever ships, so adding themes/<name>.css needs
   *  no edit here. THIS LIST IS THE COMPLETE SET OF BRAND-OVERRIDE
   *  SELECTORS — a new one must be added here too, or its subtree will
   *  render the parent's semantics over the child's brand.
   * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  :root,
  .dark,
  [data-scheme='dark'],
  [data-theme] {
    --primary: var(--interlace-primary);
    --primary-foreground: var(--interlace-primary-foreground);
    --background: var(--interlace-background);
    --foreground: var(--interlace-foreground);
    --card: var(--interlace-card);
    --card-foreground: var(--interlace-card-foreground);
    --popover: var(--interlace-popover);
    --popover-foreground: var(--interlace-popover-foreground);
    --muted: var(--interlace-muted);
    --muted-foreground: var(--interlace-muted-foreground);
    --accent: var(--interlace-accent);
    --accent-foreground: var(--interlace-accent-foreground);
    --secondary: var(--interlace-secondary);
    --secondary-foreground: var(--interlace-secondary-foreground);
    --border: var(--interlace-border);
    --input: var(--interlace-input);
    --ring: var(--interlace-ring);
    --destructive: var(--interlace-destructive);
    --destructive-foreground: var(--interlace-destructive-foreground);

    /* Status semantics — NEW. Surfaces success / warning / info as
     * shadcn-bare token names so consumers reach for `bg-success`,
     * `text-warning`, `bg-info` instead of `bg-emerald-700` /
     * `bg-amber-500` / `bg-blue-600`. Brand fork-friendly: override
     * `--interlace-success` / `-warning` / `-info` in
     * `@layer interlace.brand` to swap the underlying hex. */
    --success: var(--interlace-success);
    --success-foreground: var(--interlace-success-foreground);
    --warning: var(--interlace-warning);
    --warning-foreground: var(--interlace-warning-foreground);
    --info: var(--interlace-info);
    --info-foreground: var(--interlace-info-foreground);
    --caution: var(--interlace-caution);
    --caution-foreground: var(--interlace-caution-foreground);

    --scrim: var(--interlace-scrim);
    --scrim-foreground: var(--interlace-scrim-foreground);
    --hero-star: var(--interlace-hero-star);
    --hero-trail: var(--interlace-hero-trail);
    --hero-meteor: var(--interlace-hero-meteor);
    --hero-surface: var(--interlace-hero-surface);
    --hero-surface-deep: var(--interlace-hero-surface-deep);
    --hero-foreground: var(--interlace-hero-foreground);

    /* Window-control dots — unprefixed names so the CodeWindow chrome can be
     * lifted into a consumer that defines only these three properties. */
    --window-control-close: var(--interlace-window-control-close);
    --window-control-minimize: var(--interlace-window-control-minimize);
    --window-control-zoom: var(--interlace-window-control-zoom);

    /* Chart palette — semantic aliases of the brand layer. Overrides
     * the bridge layer (theme.css) values, so a consumer who wants
     * different chart hues forks `@layer interlace.brand` to set
     * `--interlace-chart-N` and the `--chart-N` token flows through. */
    --chart-1: var(--interlace-chart-1);
    --chart-2: var(--interlace-chart-2);
    --chart-3: var(--interlace-chart-3);
    --chart-4: var(--interlace-chart-4);
    --chart-5: var(--interlace-chart-5);

    /* Visualisation semantics — the chart's non-series vocabulary.
     *
     * Declared HERE and not in `theme.css`, on purpose: `--chart-N` is a
     * shadcn-bare name the bridge layer must supply for stock shadcn chart
     * code, but `--viz-*` is Interlace-original. `index.css` imports both, so
     * every consumer on the canonical one-line import gets it.
     *
     * Three resolve to brand hex (grid / axis / edge — contrast tables above).
     * Every other one is an ALIAS of a token whose contrast is already verified
     * in both themes. Deliberate: a diverging red/green scale that drifts away
     * from `--success` / `--destructive` is how a product ends up with two
     * greens that mean "good". One fork surface, one green. */
    --viz-grid: var(--interlace-viz-grid);
    --viz-axis: var(--interlace-viz-axis);
    --viz-edge: var(--interlace-viz-edge);

    /* Meaning-bearing marks — each an existing, verified token. */
    --viz-edge-active: var(--primary);
    --viz-node: var(--muted-foreground);
    --viz-node-active: var(--primary);
    --viz-crosshair: var(--muted-foreground);

    /* Direction. NOTE FOR COMPONENT AUTHORS: colour must never be the only
     * signal — red/green is invisible to ~8% of men. Every component using
     * these also prints a sign, an arrow, or a shape. See
     * docs/philosophies/VISUALIZATION_PHILOSOPHY.md. */
    --viz-positive: var(--success);
    --viz-negative: var(--destructive);
    --viz-neutral: var(--muted-foreground);

    /* Threshold / target bands drawn behind the series. Alpha-composited off
     * `--foreground` so it tracks the theme instead of needing a pair. */
    --viz-band: color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 6%, transparent);

    /* Annotations — an action drawn ON the curve. Three kinds, three verified
     * hues, distinguished by marker SHAPE as well as hue (shape is what
     * survives greyscale). */
    --viz-annotation-publish: var(--primary);
    --viz-annotation-release: var(--info);
    --viz-annotation-action: var(--warning);

    /* Override fumadocs-prefixed tokens for AA contrast.
     *
     * Fumadocs `neutral.css` ships `--color-fd-muted-foreground: #737373`,
     * which yields 4.34–4.46:1 contrast against the `bg-fd-card/40-50`
     * surfaces our Section / SectionHeader stories render — just below
     * the WCAG 2.2 AA 4.5:1 floor and gates Storybook a11y CI red.
     *
     * Rebinding to the brand muted-foreground (a darker warm grey in
     * light, lighter in dark) clears the threshold and keeps brand
     * consistency between shadcn-styled and fumadocs-styled surfaces.
     */
    --color-fd-muted-foreground: var(--interlace-muted-foreground);

    /* Brand mark bar fills — the UNPREFIXED names are the cross-repo
     * contract: brand-logo.tsx and the eslint docs site both read
     * `var(--brand-mark-bar-*)`, so a consumer outside this monorepo can
     * define just these two properties and render the same lockup. */
    --brand-mark-bar-o: var(--interlace-brand-mark-bar-o);
    --brand-mark-bar-g: var(--interlace-brand-mark-bar-g);
  }
}

/* Register the shadcn-bare tokens as Tailwind v4 theme keys so utilities
 * like `bg-card`, `text-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary` are
 * generated. `inline` preserves the `var()` reference, so the runtime
 * `.dark { --background: ... }` overrides above flow through to every
 * utility. Without this block, Tailwind v4 emits no `bg-card` rule
 * regardless of what `--card` resolves to on :root.
 *
 * STAYS AT TOP LEVEL (NOT inside `@layer`): Tailwind v4's `@theme`
 * directive is a special generator — it registers tokens AND emits
 * utility rules in Tailwind's own `theme` / `utilities` layers. Wrapping
 * it in a custom `@layer interlace.*` block breaks that processing. The
 * cascade-layer story applies to the alias bindings above, not to the
 * token-registration directive. */
@theme inline {
  --color-background: var(--background);
  --color-foreground: var(--foreground);
  --color-card: var(--card);
  --color-card-foreground: var(--card-foreground);
  --color-popover: var(--popover);
  --color-popover-foreground: var(--popover-foreground);
  --color-primary: var(--primary);
  --color-primary-foreground: var(--primary-foreground);
  --color-secondary: var(--secondary);
  --color-secondary-foreground: var(--secondary-foreground);
  --color-muted: var(--muted);
  --color-muted-foreground: var(--muted-foreground);
  --color-accent: var(--accent);
  --color-accent-foreground: var(--accent-foreground);
  --color-border: var(--border);
  --color-input: var(--input);
  --color-ring: var(--ring);
  --color-destructive: var(--destructive);
  --color-destructive-foreground: var(--destructive-foreground);

  /* Status semantics — generates bg-success, text-warning, bg-info,
   * border-info etc. */
  --color-success: var(--success);
  --color-success-foreground: var(--success-foreground);
  --color-warning: var(--warning);
  --color-warning-foreground: var(--warning-foreground);
  --color-info: var(--info);
  --color-info-foreground: var(--info-foreground);
  --color-caution: var(--caution);
  --color-caution-foreground: var(--caution-foreground);

  /* Scrim — generates bg-scrim/70, text-scrim-foreground,
   * border-scrim-foreground/30 so image-overlay surfaces stop reaching for
   * `bg-black/70` + `text-white` palette escapes. */
  --color-scrim: var(--scrim);
  --color-scrim-foreground: var(--scrim-foreground);

  /* Cosmic-hero surface — generates bg-hero-surface / text-hero-foreground
   * so HeroCosmic paints its always-dark surface from tokens instead of
   * `via-slate-950 to-black` palette escapes. */
  --color-hero-surface: var(--hero-surface);
  --color-hero-surface-deep: var(--hero-surface-deep);
  --color-hero-foreground: var(--hero-foreground);

  /* Window-control dots — generates bg-window-control-close etc. so the
   * CodeWindow chrome stays inside the Tailwind utility surface (R18/R19)
   * instead of reaching for `bg-[#ff5f57]`. */
  --color-window-control-close: var(--window-control-close);
  --color-window-control-minimize: var(--window-control-minimize);
  --color-window-control-zoom: var(--window-control-zoom);

  /* Chart palette utilities — generates bg-chart-1, text-chart-2,
   * border-chart-3 etc. Already declared in theme.css (bridge layer);
   * re-declared here at semantics-layer priority so brand overrides
   * propagate. */
  --color-chart-1: var(--chart-1);
  --color-chart-2: var(--chart-2);
  --color-chart-3: var(--chart-3);
  --color-chart-4: var(--chart-4);
  --color-chart-5: var(--chart-5);

  /* Visualisation utilities — generates stroke-viz-axis, fill-viz-band,
   * text-viz-positive, bg-viz-grid etc. Charts are SVG, so `stroke-*` and
   * `fill-*` are the utilities actually used; Tailwind emits them from the
   * same `--color-*` registration as `bg-*` / `text-*`. */
  --color-viz-grid: var(--viz-grid);
  --color-viz-axis: var(--viz-axis);
  --color-viz-edge: var(--viz-edge);
  --color-viz-edge-active: var(--viz-edge-active);
  --color-viz-node: var(--viz-node);
  --color-viz-node-active: var(--viz-node-active);
  --color-viz-crosshair: var(--viz-crosshair);
  --color-viz-positive: var(--viz-positive);
  --color-viz-negative: var(--viz-negative);
  --color-viz-neutral: var(--viz-neutral);
  --color-viz-band: var(--viz-band);
  --color-viz-annotation-publish: var(--viz-annotation-publish);
  --color-viz-annotation-release: var(--viz-annotation-release);
  --color-viz-annotation-action: var(--viz-annotation-action);
}

## @interlace/theme

Five stylesheets landed in `styles/interlace/`, in cascade order: tokens.css → foundation.css → preflight.css → theme.css → interlace-theme.css → themes/harbor.css.

Import them from your global stylesheet in exactly that order.

Full contract: https://ds.interlace.tools/css-contract
